title: Ali's death
hook: Ali is struck in the mosque at Kufa during Ramadan, and asks that his killer be treated fairly (reported)

segments.voice: Yesterday, the shield and the judge: Ali took his claim to court and lost for lack of a witness. Your line was the caliph lost the case. Did you let a fair decision go against you? Day eight hundred eighty-six.

A man named Ibn Muljam is in the mosque at Kufa, and he has a sword. He is one of the Kharijites, the ones who declared Ali an unbeliever for agreeing to talk at Siffin. It is Ramadan, still dark, and people are coming in for the dawn prayer. Ali, the caliph, is among them. Umar fell at this same hour, in Medina. Now, at the dawn prayer in Kufa, Ibn Muljam strikes Ali on the head. The wound is deep. Ali is carried home. What he says in the days that follow is the reason this lesson exists.
screen: `DARK, AND RAMADAN.` → `A SWORD AT DAWN PRAYER.` → `CARRIED HOME.`

segments.voice: Reports say that when he was struck, Ali said: by the Lord of the Ka'bah, I have won. Shia and Sunni sources both carry versions of this. A man struck down at prayer, in the month of fasting, counting it as victory. Then come his instructions about the man who did it. The histories, and the letter of counsel to his sons Hasan and Husayn kept in Nahj al-Balagha, give them like this. Keep him well. Feed him, and give him somewhere decent to stay. If I live, I will decide what to do with him; I may forgive him. If I die, then one blow for one blow. Do not kill anyone else on my account. And do not mutilate him, because the Prophet, peace be upon him, forbade mutilation, even of a rabid dog. Set that against the times. A city in turmoil. A ruler killed by a man who called him an unbeliever. And the dying man's worry is that his own side might go too far. No mob. No revenge on a whole tribe. Only what the law allows, and nothing beyond it, with forgiveness left open. That is your line: fair to his killer. Ali died of the wound soon after. Sunni Muslims honor him as the fourth of the rightly guided caliphs. Shia Muslims mourn him as the first Imam, and they observe the nights of his wounding and his death in Ramadan with prayer and grief. His shrine at Najaf, in Iraq, is where Shia Muslims hold he is buried, and pilgrims go there. The fitnah was not over, but this is how Ali left it.
screen: `I HAVE WON, BY THE LORD OF THE KA'BAH.` · `FEED HIM. KEEP HIM WELL.` · `ONE BLOW FOR ONE BLOW, NO MORE.` · `MOURNED IN RAMADAN.` · then, large: `FAIR TO HIS KILLER.`

segments.voice: The practice: be fair even to an enemy. Settle, and breathe. Bring to mind someone who has wronged you, a real wrong, not a small one. Breathe in, and notice what you'd like to happen to them. Then ask the narrower question Ali asked: what would actually be fair? Not more. Breathe out, and let go of the part that goes beyond fair, the extra blow, the story told to everyone, the punishment of people around them. If you pray, you can leave the rest with God. The bell holds the time.

Ali's death. Struck at the dawn prayer in the mosque at Kufa in Ramadan by a Kharijite, he asked, the reports say, that his killer be kept well and treated within the law, and no further. Today's word.
Your line: fair to his killer. Today, when you talk about someone who has hurt you, say only what is true and fair, and leave out the extra. Day eight hundred eighty-six.

howItsDone: Shia Muslims mourn Ali's wounding and death on nights of Ramadan with prayer and gatherings and visit his shrine at Najaf; Sunni Muslims honor him as the fourth rightly guided caliph and retell his instructions about his killer.

original.note: Arabic: by the Lord of the Ka'bah, I have won; words reported from Ali when he was struck.

trapdoor: what you thought: Ali died in battle.
what it means: he was struck at the dawn prayer in Kufa by a Kharijite, and asked that his killer be kept well and treated within the law.
what a scholar hears: the reported words 'I have won, by the Lord of the Ka'bah', and his counsel to Hasan and Husayn in Nahj al-Balagha forbidding mutilation and revenge on others.

notes: Audit: garbled 'Hold that against the times' fixed to 'Set that against the times'. 'Feed him, give him somewhere decent to stay' comes from the histories rather than Nahj al-Balagha letter 47; the teach credits both together, confirm.
The outline marks the instructions as 'reported'; the script attributes them to the histories and Nahj al-Balagha letter 47 (numbering varies by edition). Confirm wording and sources.
'By the Lord of the Ka'bah, I have won' is reported in Shia sources and some Sunni ones; the script says 'Shia and Sunni sources both carry versions of this'. Confirm.

'A few days later' and 'the fourth of the rightly guided caliphs': confirm these are acceptable under the claims rule (the four are a standard Sunni designation already used on day 881). Specific Ramadan dates are omitted on purpose.
Najaf: Shia Muslims hold he is buried there; some Sunni traditions name other places. The script attributes the burial site to Shia belief only.
Ibn Muljam is identified as a Kharijite, which ties back to day 884; confirm.

Editor: the hook opened almost exactly like day 876's (dark mosque, dawn prayer, a caliph struck); it now opens on Ibn Muljam and names the echo of Umar's death plainly. 'A few days later' cut to 'soon after' under the claims rule.
